title: Electricity and Magnets
introductionText:
Physics
Electricity and Magnets
Start with this, every single time
"Electricity is very useful, but it is dangerous. We never put our fingers, or anything else, into a socket. Only grown‑ups plug things in. We
never touch electrical things with wet hands."
The Big Idea — part 1: Some things need electricity to work. Some get it from the wall socket, and some get it from a battery.
The Big Idea — part 2: A magnet pulls (attracts) objects made of iron and steel only. It does not attract every metal, and it never attracts
plastic, wood, paper or fabric.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"A long time ago there was no electricity. To see at night, people lit a lantern with fire. To clean the floor, they used a broom. To write a
letter, they used a pen. Now we press one switch and the lamp comes on. That is electricity doing the work for us."
Before electricity Today, with electricity
lantern with a flame lamp
broom vacuum cleaner
washing dishes by hand dishwasher
typewriter computer
hand whisk electric mixer
Try It at Home
The magnet hunt — and the big surprise
Take a fridge magnet around the house. Test a key, a spoon, a coin, an iron nail, a plastic button, a leaf, a piece of aluminium foil, a gold or
silver ring. He predicts each one first.
Here is the surprise: aluminium foil is metal, and gold is metal — but the magnet completely ignores them. So "it is metal" is not the right
answer. The right answer is: a magnet only pulls iron and steel. Let him discover this himself; do not tell him first.
+ −
a battery never touch a socket iron and steel only
torch, toy car, clock
Three things to remember from this unit: batteries, socket safety, and what magnets really pull.
More examples to talk about
Plug, battery, or neither? Sort these three ways: the fridge (plug), a wall clock (battery), a bicycle (neither), a mobile phone (battery, then
plug to charge), a book (neither), the air conditioner (plug), a torch (battery), a chair (neither).
Where do we already use magnets? The fridge door seal, fridge magnets, a magnetic screwdriver, the catch on a cupboard door, the
closure on a handbag, headphones, some toys.
A magnet through things: put a paper clip on a sheet of paper and move a magnet underneath. The clip moves! A magnet can pull through
paper, cloth and even a thin plastic box.
iron / steel
Key Words
electricity appliance battery switch magnet attract iron steel magnetic

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Tick (✓) the things that need electricity to work:
television book vacuum cleaner lantern lamp chair dishwasher
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Need electricity: television, vacuum cleaner, lamp, dishwasher. Do not: book, lantern (it uses a flame), chair.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
What did people use before there was electricity?
a) instead of a lamp
b) instead of a vacuum cleaner
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) a lantern or a candle b) a broom

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Yes or no?
a) A magnet attracts all metals. YES / NO
b) A magnet does not attract all metals. YES / NO
c) A magnet attracts only metals made from iron or steel. YES / NO
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) NO b) YES c) YES

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Circle the objects a magnet will pull:
steel key plastic button iron nail sock steel coat hanger leaf aluminium foil
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: The magnet pulls: steel key, iron nail, steel coat hanger. It does not pull the plastic button, the sock, the leaf or the aluminium foil.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Some things work without a wall socket because they have a inside.
Write the most important safety rule about electricity.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Never put fingers or objects into a socket; only a grown‑up plugs things in; never touch electrical things with wet hands.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Sort these: fridge, wall clock, bicycle, torch, book, air conditioner
Uses a plug Uses a battery Uses neither
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Plug: fridge, air conditioner. Battery: wall clock, torch. Neither: bicycle, book.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Name two places in your home where a magnet is being used.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any two: fridge magnets, the seal on the fridge door, a cupboard door catch, a handbag clasp, a magnetic screwdriver, headphones.
